description.purpose: Search Notion pages and databases the integration has access to by free-text query.
when_to_use: When the user wants to find a page or database by partial title.
When the exact id is unknown.
limitations: Only objects shared with the integration are visible.
Returns at most 100 results per call (Notion API limit).
Search index lag of up to 60s for new pages.
description.parameter_overview: Single `query` string; results returned as smart IDs of the form notion-prod-notion:object:Page:{uuid} or notion-prod-notion:object:Database:{uuid}, ranked by relevance.

truncation.guidance_template: Showing {N} of {Total} matches. Use `cursor` to paginate or refine your query.

description.purpose: Fetch the full Notion object addressed by a smart ID (Page or Database).
when_to_use: When you have a smart ID returned by `search` or `list_objects`.
When you need the full property set of a page or database.
limitations: Returns only objects the integration can access.
Page property values may include rich text — can be large.
description.parameter_overview: Single `id` string in the smart-ID format `notion-prod-notion:object:{Page|Database}:{uuid}`; routing maps the type to the correct Notion endpoint.

truncation.guidance_template: Object exceeded {threshold} tokens; {N} fields included. Re-call with `properties` projection.

description.purpose: List the Notion databases the integration has access to (each database is a collection of pages).
when_to_use: At session start to discover what databases the user can read.
When mapping a free-text request to a specific database id.
limitations: Only databases shared with the integration are visible.
Returns metadata only — use `list_objects` to enumerate rows.
description.parameter_overview: Optional `pattern` (glob on database title) and `include_schema` (bool) for embedding the property schema; defaults return all visible databases without schema.

truncation.guidance_template: Listed {N} databases. Use `pattern` to narrow by title.

description.purpose: List Notion pages within a chosen database with filter, sort, projection, and cursor pagination.
when_to_use: When enumerating rows of a known Notion database.
When server-side filter (e.g., status=Done) or sort is needed.
when_not_to_use: When you have an explicit page id — use `fetch`.
When the database id is unknown — use `search` or `list_collections` first.
limitations: Cursor pagination only; max 100 rows per call.
Filter expressions limited to Notion's documented filter shape (property/operator/value).

truncation.guidance_template: Returned {N} of approximately {Total} pages. Use `cursor` to paginate or `properties` to project fewer fields.

description.purpose: Create a new Notion page or update an existing one (smart routing by id presence).
when_to_use: When inserting a new row into a Notion database.
When patching property values on an existing page.
limitations: Cannot upsert into a Database object — only Page objects.
Property values must conform to the parent database's schema; mismatches fail with 400.
Re-creating with the same external id will produce a duplicate page (Notion has no unique constraints).
description.parameter_overview: `collection` is the parent database id. Provide `data.parent` and `data.properties` for create; `id` + `data.properties` for update. Notion does not enforce uniqueness server-side.

truncation.guidance_template: {action} succeeded for page {id}. Refetch with `properties` projection if response was truncated.

description.purpose: Archive a Notion page (Notion does not hard-delete; archive is the canonical removal operation).
when_to_use: When removing a row from a Notion database without permanent loss.
When cleaning up test pages on a sandbox database.
limitations: Implements archive, not hard delete. Archived pages can be restored via `upsert` with `data.archived: false`.
Cannot archive a Database object via this tool — must be done from the Notion UI.
Re-archiving an archived page is a no-op (idempotent).
description.parameter_overview: `type: 'object'` + `id` (smart ID of Page) + `confirm: true`. Batch archive supported via `ids` array.

truncation.guidance_template: Archived {deleted_count} of {requested} pages. Pages can be restored via `upsert` with archived=false.
